literal: Having seen, heard, tasted, smelt, and touched, all five perceiving senses are present indeed within this bright-braceleted woman.
translation: The pleasures of all five senses—sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch—are found together in this woman adorned with bright bracelets.
modern: பார்த்தல், கேட்டல், உண்ணல், மோத்தல், தொடுதல் ஆகிய ஐந்து புலன்களாலும் அறியப்படும் இன்பங்கள் அனைத்தும் ஒளி பொருந்திய வளையல்களை அணிந்த இவளிடத்தே மட்டுமே உள்ளன.
explanation: This couplet celebrates the ultimate sensory fulfillment found in the beloved. The poet lists the five modes of perception: seeing (kaṇṭu), hearing (kēṭṭu), tasting (uṇṭu), smelling (uyirttu), and touching (uṟṟu). While these five senses (aimpulanum) usually seek gratification from different sources, the lover experiences them all simultaneously in the presence of his beloved, referred to metonymically as the one wearing bright bracelets (oṇtoṭi). The sandhi of 'oḷ' (bright) and 'toṭi' (bracelet) naturally yields 'oṇtoṭi' through standard Tamil sound-merging rules.
